title: $x^p-t$ is irreducible when $t$ has no $p$-th root
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, $F$ a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p$, and $t\in F$ an element which is not a $p$-th power in $F$ (there is no $c\in F$ with $c^p=t$). Then the polynomial $x^p-t$ of the polynomial ring $F[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is irreducible: it is not a unit of $F[x]$, and whenever $x^p-t=gh$ with $g,h\in F[x]$, one of $g,h$ is a unit of $F[x]$, i.e. a nonzero constant polynomial.
